answer_1.quote: We evaluate our method on both human and automated benchmarks, measuring the content‑independence, quality, and utility of STYLEDISTANCE embeddings. By creating near‑exact paraphrases with controlled stylistic variations, we produce positive and negative examples across 40 distinct style features.
answer_1.outputs: synthetic paraphrases with controlled style variations and learned style embeddings

answer_2.quote: We also run automatic evaluations to assess other properties of the dataset: Content Similarity measures the average semantic similarity between the positive and negative parallel examples; Fluency measures the average fluency of our examples using a classifier trained on CoLA; Diversity uses the score proposed to measure how different each generated text is from every other in terms of content/topic using semantic similarity.

answer_4.quote: First, we measured the extent to which humans judge our positive examples do contain the desired style feature and our negative examples do not. ... annotators judged the positive and negative labels correct 92% of the time.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to verify whether the positive sentence exhibits the target style feature and whether the negative sentence does not, based on the provided style definitions.
criteria: absence of target style feature in negative example
